answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. The kernel is the held bond, the nebula the tenure multiplier, and the atlas the convex curve they ride; the kernel can be split but the nebula does not divide, and the atlas punishes the split. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
